title: The Key to the Hall
subtitle: 责任担当 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）
meta: 主题语境：责任担当（做人与做事·责任与担当）　|　核心词汇：charge　|　正文 351 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 charge 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In my second year the teacher ① in charge of the school hall handed me a key. 'You are ② in charge of the lights,' she said, and then she left for a fortnight. Nobody had ever asked me to be responsible for anything important, and I did not sleep well for two nights.

The first problem was money. I was told that there is a ③ charge of two hundred yuan an evening for letting the hall. When the dance club arrived, nobody had explained this to them and they thought the room was free. They argued, and one man said we had no right to charge them anything at all. I wrote out a receipt by hand and apologised twice.

The second problem was worse. One Saturday the speakers would not start. An electrician came, looked at the battery and said it simply had not been ④ charged since June. He also said something I have never forgotten: 'Nobody ever gets praised for ⑤ charging a battery. They only notice when it is flat.'

Then a pipe burst and we were told the hall must close for repairs. A local newspaper even suggested that whoever had neglected the building should be ⑥ charged with damaging public property. No formal ⑦ charge was ever made, but I lay awake wondering whether that somebody was me. The head teacher called me in. 'Who put you in charge here?' she asked. 'You did,' I answered. 'Then tell me, were you paid?' Not a penny, I said. There is no duty, she replied, without somebody willing to be ⑧ charged nothing for carrying it.

The repairs took a month. When the hall reopened I made a list: check the battery every Friday, keep two receipts, and never let anybody ⑨ charge through the back door without asking. Responsibility, I realised, is mostly a list, and mostly boring; nobody is in charge of anything they have not checked with their own hands. Nobody praises such lists, and nobody ever will; I still keep mine, six years later, for the sake of ten hundred lights somebody else will never ⑩ charge me with having neglected.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 负责；掌管（in charge of / take charge of）
F. v. 指控；控告（charge sb with sth）
H. 固定搭配：be charged nothing / free of charge 免费

items.q: the teacher in charge of the school hall
You are in charge of the lights
a charge of two hundred yuan an evening
we had no right to charge them anything at all
it simply had not been charged since June
Nobody ever gets praised for charging a battery
No formal charge was ever made
willing to be charged nothing for carrying it
let anybody charge through the back door

answers.why: in charge of＋事物作后置定语修饰 teacher，意为“负责学校礼堂的老师”。
be in charge of 表示“负责、掌管”，这里指由我负责灯光，是全文责任的起点。
a charge of＋金额，是名词“费用”，指租用礼堂每晚两百元。
charge sb＋金额，作动词“向某人收费”，对方认为房间本该免费。
had not been charged 为被动语态，主语是电池，指“未曾充电”，是电工检查后的结论。
charging a battery 是动名词，仍是“给电池充电”，与第 5 题同义复现。
be charged with＋罪名，意为“被指控犯有……”，报纸认为疏于管理的人应被追责。
a formal charge 是名词“正式的指控”，与前一句的动词 charged 形成名动呼应。
be charged nothing 意为“一分钱也不收”，与 free of charge 同义，指有人愿意无偿承担。
charge through＋地点，是动词“冲、冲进”，这里指未经询问从后门闯进来。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 负责学校礼堂的老师把钥匙交给了我。（in charge of）
租用礼堂的费用是每晚两百元。（charge n.）
我们没有权利向他们收任何钱。（charge v.）
那块电池从六月起就没有充过电。（charge v.）
有人建议起诉那个忽视建筑的人。（charge sb with）
孩子们从后门冲了进来。（charge v.）
answers: The teacher in charge of the school hall handed me the key.
The charge for letting the hall is two hundred yuan an evening.
We had no right to charge them anything at all.
The battery had not been charged since June.
Some people suggested charging whoever had neglected the building with damaging public property.
The children charged in through the back door.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 charge 的 3 种不同用法；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: When the teacher in charge of the hall handed me the key, I took charge of nothing but the lights.
I soon learned that the charge for letting the hall is two hundred yuan an evening, and that arguing helps nobody.
Nobody ever wins praise for charging a battery; they only notice when the hall goes dark.
Some people even thought whoever neglected the building should be charged with damaging public property.
To this day I am charged nothing for the work, and I would refuse pay if it were offered.
Responsibility is mostly a short list kept honestly, and mostly boring — check the battery, keep the receipt, mind the lights.
